item.title: Multi‐Scale Assessment of Population Exposure to Landslides in Vietnam
item.description:
Xinrui Lu, Jiahui Zhang, Qigen Lin, Shicong Ren, Haoyuan Hong
Transactions in GIS, vol. 30, issue 7
DOI: 10.1111/tgis.70379
ABSTRACT Vietnam's complex terrain and monsoon climate create extensive landslide‐prone conditions, yet the population exposure patterns of its urban, rural, and demographic groups remain insufficiently quantified. This study combines the Global Landslide Non‐Susceptibility Map (GLNSM), high‐resolution population layers, urban–rural settlement data, and GADM administrative boundaries in ArcGIS 10.8 to estimate population exposure to landslide‐prone areas from the national scale to the district scale. Areas outside the GLNSM non‐susceptible class were treated as potentially landslide‐prone and overlaid with population grids. Results show that landslide‐prone zones cover approximately 107,491 km 2 , or 32.63% of Vietnam's land area, mainly in the Northeast, Northwest, North Central, South Central, and Central Highlands regions. Approximately 4.35 million people, or 4.47% of the national population, are exposed. Rural exposure is broader than urban exposure, while district‐level hotspots such as Mong Duong, Bai Chay, and Ward 7 reveal local concentrations that can be masked by provincial aggregation. Demographic overlays indicate differential exposure among men, women, women aged 15–49, adolescents, older adults, and children under five, and children under five showed the highest exposure rate among the examined demographic groups. The study demonstrates how multi‐scale GIS overlay can support spatially targeted landslide mitigation in data‐limited settings.

item.title: A Multi‐Objective Optimization Framework for Locating Metro Stations by Integrating Travel Demand, Accessibility, and Land Use Intensity
item.description:
Xiping Yang, Jiayu Liu, Wei Tu, Zhiyuan Zhao, Rui An, Jiyuan Li, Xiaoyan Huang
Transactions in GIS, vol. 30, issue 7
DOI: 10.1111/tgis.70404
ABSTRACT Transit‐Oriented Development (TOD) strategies help to achieve sustainable transportation and vibrant communities. The selection of suitable locations for metro stations plays a fundamental role in implementing TOD planning. However, current research predominantly focuses on evaluating existing metro stations, often overlooking the critical task of optimally locating new ones. This study proposes a multi‐objective optimization framework for locating urban metro stations based on the concept of TOD, which takes three key dimensions: travel demand, functional accessibility, and land use intensity into consideration. We develop an iterative optimization process by combining a greedy search method with an elite fast non‐dominated sorting genetic algorithm (NSGA‐II) to search for solutions that satisfy the three objectives. The proposed model is validated through a case study in Xi'an, China, where its feasibility is assessed by designing various scenarios. The results indicate that the model can effectively identify optimal locations for metro stations under multiple objectives. Therefore, the proposed method can be used to assist urban planners in identifying suitable locations for transit stations.
